The Savoy Male and Female College      59

Typical Lower-class Recitations.—A typical lower-class recitation began, according to descriptions of ex-students, with the teacher's command to, "Come forward, please!" This order meant that the class should step up to the "recitation benches" at the front of the room and facing the rostrum. The person reciting was expected to step up on the rostrum where he could be seen and heard by all. If the class happened to be a Spelling class, a chalk line was drawn along a plank on the floor and the pupils were called to "Toe the Line." The teachers' rules required that, in order to keep a straight and orderly line, the pupils' toes should reach to, and not over, the line at once. If a student persisted in stretching one or both arms and squirming about, the teacher sternly repeated his request to "Toe the line, please."

    The old Webster "Blue-back" Speller was used altogether and when a new spelling rule was being taught, the method is, if the word were several syllables long, then each syllable when spelled was pronounced separately, with more and more syllables after and including each syllable finished until the last syllable was spelled and pronounced, then the whole word was pronounced—and the pupil, if successful, breathed more easily. If not successful, he went to the foot to wait until his neighbor in line had succeeded and then "turned him down." If the pupil happened to be learning a primer or serial, a glib speller's recitation became a foreign-sounding succession of syllable-and-sound combinations, e. g., aigh; z, az, aigh-er; r, rlit; aigh-er(h); a, t, at; aigh-er-hat.
